content.text: Stars, our pet community's first group purchase was a success. How about we, the core organizers, have a small thank-you dinner? From setting up social media accounts for the 'boss' to planning the offline meetup 'Social Shiba vs. Aloof Ragdoll' and building the fan community, everyone has really worked hard. What would you like to eat? I've created a poll to gather everyone's opinions.

Haha, Xiaomeng, you're always so thoughtful! But voting is such a hassle—let's just decide directly. I've bookmarked a trendy themed restaurant with an environment perfect for taking photos. I'll send it to you. Remember that lively poster you made when we were planning the pet social event? This dinner gathering needs to have that same eye-catching vibe.
Alright, then send it to me and let me have a look.

Look, this Chinese-themed restaurant has such a vibe with its decorations, and the lighting design is absolutely stunning. It’s just like the aesthetic style of the game skins we had before—you’d definitely love it. It reminds me of that green long-haired skin with petal effects you collected, and the sci-fi style skin for Lan that I shared. They’re all such a visual treat.

Wow, this restaurant is really beautiful, kind of reminiscent of the luxurious feel of the Lan skin effect you shared before. But we should consider everyone's tastes and budget, right? There are many options in the poll, like hotpot or private kitchen dishes, which might be more popular. Just like when we chose the script for our last 'beginner session' of script murder, we need to accommodate different preferences and not just go for what looks good.

Then take a look at this one. This is a Cantonese restaurant with a great atmosphere and highly-rated dishes. Plus, it has private rooms, perfect for us to have fun without worrying about small accidents like the "boss" getting too excited and knocking over a cup, just like during pet meetups at a café.

Well, having a private room is indeed nice—it helps avoid the noise and crowds like in a beginner's script-killing session. What about the budget? Let's not go too expensive, since we're just starting out. Remember when you shared the script-killing price list before, you even said it was much cheaper than skins? This time, we should also be practical.

No problem, I've checked it out. The per-person cost is moderate, and it offers great value for money. Plus, the atmosphere is unique—taking photos and sharing them on social media can attract more followers, just like how the "Boss's" social butterfly moment meme went viral, increasing exposure. Hasn't our pet community grown from a few thousand to nearly fifty thousand followers? This gathering can also serve as high-quality content.

Alright, let's settle on this one! You always come up with interesting ideas, from carrying me in games and sharing hero rankings to planning pet events and inviting me to scripted murder mystery games. How about scheduling it for next Saturday evening? The participants will be just our core organizers, around 5-6 people. We can also invite that logical genius friend from the last scripted murder mystery group—he probably contributed a lot too.

Perfect! I'm free next Saturday night, and I'll be as punctual as when we schedule gaming sessions. By the way, just eating at the gathering would be boring—how about adding some mini-games? I can totally get into character and lead the fun, just like during my live streams. I promise to keep the atmosphere lively and banish boredom!

Haha, I knew you’d never settle for boring! I have an idea: a number-guessing game. It’s simple, easy to play, and can really liven things up. Let me send you the rules to check out. I feel like a game that requires a bit of logic would be perfect for our group—from gaming to script murder mysteries to pet operations.

Look, this game involves narrowing down the range to guess a number based on hints, which requires a bit of logic, similar to how you analyze the battlefield in your games. It also reminds me of the comparison table you made when we were choosing a script for the murder mystery game—it was so well-organized and helped everyone make quick decisions.

Oh, this sounds fun! It's like the interactivity we set up when planning pet events, such as the 'Most Adorable Contrast Award.' I get the rules now—everyone takes turns guessing, and the loser performs or shares something interesting. How about sharing funny stories about our pets, or anecdotes like the ones we discussed before, such as losing streaks in games or sharing skin collections?

Okay, sure! But let's not go overboard—harmony is key. Remember the humor you bring to your game streams; just keep it in moderation. I'll notify the participants, including that logical-minded friend from the last script murder group. He’ll probably enjoy this kind of game. From gaming to script murder, and now to this gathering, our little group is really growing!

No problem! Then I'll take care of the restaurant reservation and game props preparation. The process roughly goes like this: dinner, chatting, playing games, and taking photos for keepsakes. Just like how we've evolved from gaming partners to event planning partners, and then to an entertainment exploration team, this time it's even more relaxed, purely to thank and celebrate our shared "growth"—from your losing streak in games to me carrying you to victory, and then turning "Boss" into an internet sensation.

Yes, this time is mainly about expressing gratitude and relaxing. Xingchen, thank you for always being so supportive. From comforting me after losing streaks in games and sending me hero rankings, to managing pet communities and planning beginner sessions for scripted murder mysteries, you always make things interesting, truly embodying the principle of "fun first."

Xiaomeng, you're just the same—warm and reliable! From meticulously planning the pet event schedule and risk management to researching scripted murder mystery genres and maintaining community harmony, you are the key to making everything 'perfect.' So it's settled: next Saturday evening, at the Cantonese restaurant, with 5-6 core organizers, and a number-guessing game for fun. I'll send a confirmation message to the group chat using the 'Boss' account—it'll definitely have a great effect!

Great! Looking forward to the gathering, just like looking forward to every gaming session, every pet event, and every new murder mystery experience. Let's stay in touch and communicate promptly if there are any changes. Grow together, and prioritize fun above all!
